sections.changelog:
Added

  • Wrong keyboard-layout recovery: a query typed without switching layouts (e.g. "ghbdtn" for "привет", or "xt[jk" for "чехол") is detected when it returns too few results, retried in the other layout, and — only if that finds more — shown with a "Did you mean…" hint. Reuses the existing typo-correction toggle.
  • Exclude a single word from a query by prefixing it with a minus, e.g. `iphone -case` hides results that mention "case".
  • New "Exclude from search" checkbox on the post and product editor to keep an individual entry out of results.
  • Optional "Learn from clicks" ranking that gently floats the results shoppers actually pick for a query. Off by default, capped so it can never outrank a better match, and safe on fresh catalogs.
  • No-results contact button: show a configurable call-to-action (phone, WhatsApp or any link) under "Nothing found" to recover visitors who don't find what they searched for.
  • One-click merchandising from the Analytics tab: each query row can pre-fill a synonym, redirect or pin starter on the Relevance tab.
  • Optional weekly search-digest email with the top and no-result queries. Off by default.
  • Matching brands now appear as their own group in the live dropdown (with a supported brand-taxonomy plugin), alongside categories.
  • WooCommerce "Revenue by search" report (opt-in): see which searches lead to cart adds and orders, attributed to the shopper's last search before checkout. Deliberately an approximate signal, not exact accounting.

Changed

  • Ranking now saturates term frequency (BM25-style) instead of counting each repetition linearly, so a word stuffed many times into one long description can no longer outrank a clean title match. Coverage (how many distinct query words a result matches) still decides order first; a single occurrence scores exactly as before, so only heavy repetition is damped.
  • Analytics now groups similar wordings of the same query (grammatical cases and spellings) into one row, so Russian search stats stop scattering across word forms. A "Forms" column shows how many spellings folded in.
  • Field-weight and boost-strength controls are now sliders with a live value readout.
  • Visually identical Latin and Cyrillic letters in a mixed word (a/а, e/е, o/о, c/с, p/р, x/х, y/у) are unified, and a glued number+unit like "150мм" is also searchable as "150" and "мм". Run a full reindex once to apply this to existing content.
  • Product SKUs are now searchable both with and without punctuation, so "123456-123" is also found by typing "123456123". Run a full reindex once to apply this to existing products.

Fixed

  • A search for a glued number+unit such as "5000mah" now returns the matching products again instead of nothing. The automatic split into "5000" and "mah" no longer tightens the match requirement — how many words you typed decides how strict the match is, not how many index terms the split produced.
  • A minus-excluded word no longer surfaces its own category in the dropdown: "xiaomi -аккумулятор" stops showing the "Аккумуляторы" category, matching how it already drops those products.
  • The live dropdown is now an accessible combobox: the field exposes `role="combobox"` with the results as an ARIA `listbox` grouped by type, and the keyboard-highlighted result is announced to screen readers via `aria-activedescendant`/`aria-selected` while navigating with the arrow keys.
  • Products imported through MVweb Price Importer are now fully indexed. The importer writes a product's SKU, categories and attributes in a way that the standard save hook runs before they exist, so imported products used to be searchable by title only; the index now refreshes once the import finishes writing each product. Run a full reindex once after upgrading to catch products imported earlier.
  • WooCommerce products whose catalog visibility hides them from search ("Shop only" or "Hidden") are no longer indexed or returned in results, matching WooCommerce's own search behavior. Run a full reindex once to purge any already-indexed hidden products.
